💡 How to read: a higher percentile means the current gold price is more "expensive" relative to the model-implied equilibrium.
- 1-Year Percentile: short-term sentiment (fast variable)
- 3-Year Percentile: medium-term valuation position (shown in charts)
- 10-Year Percentile: the core window used by strategies
- Full History Percentile: long-cycle temperature (slow variable)
- Dual Product: 1-year percentile × full history percentile, an exploratory signal. See "What is the Dual Product" below
Zone thresholds: >90% (Extremely Overvalued) | 70%-90% (Overvalued) | 30%-70% (Fair) | 10%-30% (Undervalued) | <10% (Extremely Undervalued).

🔬 What is the "Dual Product"? (Click to expand/collapse)
① Definition
Dual Product =1-Year Percentile × Full History Percentile

For example: 1-year percentile = 0.357, full history percentile = 0.783 → Dual Product = 0.280

② Where It Comes From
All strategies based on the 10Y percentile use only a single time scale (the 10-year rolling window). A natural question: if we use signals from two time scales simultaneously—1-year (short-term sentiment) and full history (long-term valuation)—can we obtain a more robust judgment? The "Dual Product" is the exploratory answer to this question.
③ Design Logic

Both percentiles high → judged as truly overvalued (short-term and long-term signals confirm each other);
Both percentiles low → judged as truly undervalued.

④ Three Problems
⚠️ Problem 1 (Dimension): a percentile is "the rank percentage of the residual in history"; rank × rank ≠ rank. The product no longer carries "percentile" meaning.
⚠️ Problem 2 (Left-Skewed Distribution): multiplying two numbers in [0,1] always skews the result toward 0. For example, 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25, turning "Fair" into "Extremely Undervalued", systematically raising positions.
⚠️ Problem 3 (Contradictory-Signal Misjudgment): if "1-year undervalued (0.1) + full history overvalued (0.9)", the product = 0.09 is still judged "Extremely Undervalued" and leveraged up. In this most contradictory scenario, the strategy becomes most aggressive instead.
⑤ Current Market Reading
1-Year percentile = 0.357, Full History percentile = 0.783, Dual Product = 0.280.
Compared with the 10Y percentile = 0.789 (which has triggered the "Extremely Overvalued" lower bound), the Dual Product = 0.280 falls in the "Fair" zone. The two conclusions differ by a factor of 10—a direct manifestation of the Dual Product's "left-skewed distribution" problem.
⑥ Conclusion

The Dual Product is retained in the dashboard as a methodological comparison, presenting the exploration of the "multi-time-scale signal fusion" idea. For academic comparison only, not as any operational basis.

📉 Strategy Backtest & Performance

The backtest period starts after the SGE listing (from 2016-04-18). All strategies use the previous day's valuation percentile to determine the day's position, avoiding look-ahead bias. A one-way transaction cost of 0.1% and an annualized financing cost of 4.5% (only for the portion of positions > 1) have been deducted. Each strategy adopts its exhaustive optimal rebalance threshold (see details below).
📌 Note: all strategies and backtest results below are for model research display only, and do not constitute any investment advice or operational guidance.

📐 Piecewise Position Function H(q)

Input is the valuation percentile q, output is the position function value (before cap truncation)
q < 0.1 (Extremely Undervalued): Position = 3.0 - 5.0 × q → 2.5 ~ 3.0
0.1 ≤ q < 0.3 (Undervalued): Position = 2.5 - 5.0 × (q - 0.1) → 1.5 ~ 2.5
0.3 ≤ q < 0.7 (Fair): Position = 1.5 - 2.5 × (q - 0.3) → 0.5 ~ 1.5
0.7 ≤ q < 0.9 (Overvalued): Position = 0.5 - 2.0 × (q - 0.7) → 0.1 ~ 0.5
q ≥ 0.9 (Extremely Overvalued): Position = 0.1 → reduced to the minimum position

Design Rationale: the position function value is higher in undervalued zones and lower in overvalued zones. Breakpoints 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.7 / 0.9 correspond to the five valuation zones. Strategies differ in the position cap truncation (1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0).

🎯 Rebalance Thresholds by Strategy (Set to Exhaustive Optimal Values)

Rebalance threshold means: a rebalance is triggered only when the difference between the target position and the current position exceeds the threshold. A larger threshold means lower turnover and lower cost; a smaller threshold tracks signals more closely with higher turnover. Based on the Pareto optimality of exhaustive testing (9,400 combinations), this dashboard independently sets each strategy's optimal threshold:

Therefore, when the valuation percentile stays in the same zone for a long time, some strategies may show no rebalance records for consecutive weeks or even months—this is the normal behavior of the "low turnover" design, not missing data.

📌 Rebalance Day Rules: - daily: rebalance every trading day, using the previous day's percentile - weekly: rebalance every Friday (if Friday is a market holiday, no rebalance that week), using the previous day's percentile - monthly: rebalance on the last trading day of each month (must be >= the 25th), using the previous day's percentile - quarterly: rebalance on the last trading day of the quarter-end months (3/6/9/12, must be >= the 25th) - On non-rebalance days, the previous position is kept unchanged, with no transaction cost

💡 Frequency Trade-off: taking 10Y_Smart3.0 as an example—the daily version has an annualized return of 25.4% and Sharpe 1.24; the weekly version has an annualized return of 22.6% and Sharpe 1.12; the monthly version has an annualized return of 21.0% and Sharpe 1.06. The low-frequency versions achieve similar return-risk profiles with fewer trades and lower transaction costs.

📊 Gold vs. Factor Relationships

📌 Chart 1: Over the past 10 years, the gold price has climbed from about $1,200 to around 3948. The current 3-year rolling percentile is 77.9%, in the Overvalued zone. Central bank gold purchases have recently held around 52.0 tons/month.

📌 Chart 2: TIPS is currently 2.60%, and the China-U.S. yield spread is -3.28%. The latest gold-oil ratio is 41.0.

📊 Residual Trend

📌 Chart 3: The current residual is 0.0854, in the Overvalued zone.

🧠 Model Interpretation

Regression Equation: Ln(Gold) = 7.3945 + -0.3001×TIPS + -31.8011×CN_US_Spread + 0.0110×Gold_Oil_Ratio, R²=0.914

Factor Explanations:

  • TIPS (U.S. 10-Year Real Yield): Measures the opportunity cost of holding gold. Rising TIPS → gold under pressure; the coefficient is negative.
  • China-U.S. Yield Spread (CN_US_Spread): China 10-year government bond yield minus the U.S. 10-year, capturing the global capital allocation logic between China and the U.S.
  • Gold-Oil Ratio (Gold_Oil_Ratio): The price ratio of gold to WTI crude oil, reflecting risk aversion and relative valuation.

Bubble Duration:Extremely Overvalued appeared 26 times, avg 10 trading days, max 82 trading days

Residual Percentile: The current residual is 0.0854, in the Overvalued zone.
